newsitem.title: UK: OPEC NGL output to rise 160,000 bpd in 1997 - IEA.
newsitem.headline: OPEC NGL output to rise 160,000 bpd in 1997 - IEA.

text.p: OPEC's natural gas liquids (NGL) production and output of "other oils" are set to rise by 160,000 barrels per day (bpd) next year, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday. In its monthly oil market report, the IEA forecast next year's NGL output from OPEC members at 2.814 million bpd, up from 2.644 million this year and 2.417 million in 1995.
The increase will start in the fourth quarter of this year, with a 50,000 bpd rise expected.

Of this, 55 percent is expected to occur in Abu Dhabi with the completion of the first phase of the Habshan processing facility. This will handle condensates from the Bab fields' Thamama B, C and F reservoirs, the IEA said.
Qatar's output is also rising, with fourth quarter 1996 output forecast at 135,000 bpd, up from 115,000 bpd in the second quarter.
Nigeria's Oso project is due to increase NGL output by 15,000 bpd by the end of the year, but the IEA said political considerations there "create downside sensitivities."

There are also expected to be small increases of 5,000 to 10,000 bpd from Algeria, Kuwait, and Saudi Arabia, with Venezuelan Orimulsion, counted by the IEA as an "other oil", expected to raise levels by 25,000 bpd in the fourth quarter against the second quarter.
